# api-verity-lab

> API contract governance across seven formats -- OpenAPI 3.0/3.1/3.2, Swagger 2.0,
> AsyncAPI 2.x/3.x, GraphQL, gRPC and MCP tool manifests -- under one normalized
> contract model and one versioned result format. Diffs contracts, classifies
> breaking changes against 70 rules with stable ids, detects runtime drift
> against live services and recorded traffic, governs the tool surface agents call,
> and measures performance budgets.

Apache-2.0. Python 3.11+. No telemetry. Every claim in these documents is either
generated from the code or carries a dated source; counts in prose are bound to the
thing they count by a test.

## What it is for

- Failing a pull request that breaks an API contract, with the rule id and the
  non-breaking alternative.
- Telling whether a running service still matches the contract its consumers were
  given.
- Governing what an AI agent can call: tool-manifest diffing, declared-versus-live
  drift, tool-description poisoning, authentication posture, and a reviewed baseline.

## Docs

- [Rule catalog](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/rule-catalog/): Every breaking-change rule, its severity, and the non-breaking alternative
- [Spec support](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/spec-support/): Which spec versions and constructs are read, and which are not
- [Protocol support](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/protocol-support/): What each of the seven protocols supports
- [Exit codes](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/exit-codes/): The exit-code contract, and how it differs from sibling projects
- [MCP drift](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/mcp-drift/): Declared tool manifest against a running MCP server
- [MCP tool poisoning](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/mcp-poisoning/): Reading a tool description as executable text (OWASP MCP03)
- [MCP lockfile](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/mcp-lock/): A reviewed baseline for an agent's tool surface
- [MCP inventory](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/mcp-inventory/): Shadow MCP servers, found by reading client configs
- [Call budgets](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/call-budgets/): How often an agent may call each tool
- [Declared objectives](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/objectives/): `x-slo` in the contract, and why a run is a sample rather than a verdict
- [Blast radius](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/blast-radius/): Which consumers a breaking change affects
- [Ghost routes](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/ghost-routes/): Routes the contract deleted that the deployment kept
- [Inferred contracts](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/inferred-contracts/): Drafting a contract from recorded traffic
- [Monorepo sweep](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/monorepo-sweep/): Every contract in a tree, with an owner and a verdict
- [Compliance mapping](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/compliance-mapping/): Findings mapped onto OWASP MCP, Agentic and API Top 10
- [Evidence packs](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/evidence/): Dated, checksummed records for SOC 2, ISO 42001, DORA, EU AI Act
- [Audit export](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/audit-export/): The hash-chained audit log as a document checkable away from the server
- [Emergency freeze](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/kill-switch/): Stopping releases during an incident, and what a freeze does not stop
- [Migrating from oasdiff](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/oasdiff-migration/): Emitting oasdiff's own JSON shape, and which rules map onto its check ids
- [CI integration](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/ci/): Wiring the gate into a pipeline
- [Safety model](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/safety-model/): What this tool will and will not do to a target
- [Supply chain](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/supply-chain/): SBOM, SLSA provenance and pinned actions -- including what has not run yet
- [Privacy](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/privacy/): What reaches an artifact, and what never does
- [Self-hosting](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/self-hosting/): Running the server
- [SDK](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/sdk/): Using the library directly
- [Architecture](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/architecture/): How the one contract model works
- [Competitive analysis](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/competitive-analysis/): Verified, dated comparison with other tools
- [Benchmark vs oasdiff](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/benchmark/): Both engines over the same contracts, including where this one is behind

## Machine-readable

- [capabilities.json](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/capabilities.json): every command, protocol, rule id and
  exit code, generated from the code
- [result-v1 schema](https://webdevsamran.github.io/api-verity-lab/../schemas/result-v1.schema.json): the artifact contract
  every command writes

## Commands

`audit`, `baseline`, `breaking`, `budget`, `changelog`, `config`, `coverage`, `diff`, `digest`, `drift`, `evidence`, `explain`, `export`, `freeze`, `ghosts`, `infer`, `init`, `mcp-inventory`, `mcp-lock`, `mock`, `monitor`, `notify`, `plugins`, `regression`, `replay`, `report`, `rules`, `self-test`, `serve`, `server-db`, `sweep`, `test`, `validate`, `verify`, `watch`, `workflow`.

## What it does not do

- It does not authenticate, deploy, or modify a target service.
- It does not send traffic anywhere it was not explicitly pointed at, and never
  invokes an MCP tool without a named opt-in.
- It does not claim a compliance control is satisfied; it produces the records an
  auditor maps.
